claude.role: Every Claude surface that reaches this estate.
claude.why: Nothing else calls these servers, so admission is the whole perimeter. There is no second door.

mcpauth.role: Issues every token this estate accepts.
mcpauth.why: A cold start inside Claude's 10-second discovery budget is a failed sign-in, not a slow one.

google.role: Answers one question: is this a real @example.invalid person?
google.why: A Google token is never accepted here. It proves the person, and nothing else.

secrets.role: Holds the six secrets the auth server needs.
secrets.why: Keeps the signing key out of the image and out of every other service's environment.

warehouse.role: Read-only MCP over the reporting warehouse.
warehouse.why: Makes a permission a sentence about a read, rather than a grant on a dataset.

workqueue.role: Files work into the intake queue.
workqueue.why: The token is shared, so GitHub cannot say who filed anything. The audit line is the only attribution.

roster.role: Says who may do what, per service.
roster.why: Removing a row takes effect on that person's next call, not their next login.

wh.role: Holds the numbers the reports are built from.
wh.why: Read-only means the worst outcome of a bug here is a wrong answer, never a changed one.

gh.why: One token for everybody, so every allow has to be logged on our side to be attributable at all.

claudecode.role: Proves which client it is with no configuration.
claudecode.why: It has no field to type a client id into. The whole sequence exists because of that.

warehouse.why: Its refusal is how a client that knows nothing finds its way in.

mcpauth.role: Decides whether an unconfigured client may be admitted.
mcpauth.why: Makes the person the one who approves an unknown client, rather than the protocol.

claudeai.role: Publishes Claude Code's client metadata document.
claudeai.why: Which hosts may publish is the entire trust decision — it admits clients this repo has never heard of.

person.role: Meets a consent page and approves, or does not.
person.why: After an existing Google session the forward completes silently. Not asked here means never asked.

google.why: Consent precedes identity, so approving an unknown client is deliberate, not a side effect of being signed in.

audit.role: Records the two moments that matter.
audit.why: A refusal that reaches no log is a refusal nobody can count.

claude.role: Asks for a report by name.
claude.why: There is no argument that would carry SQL, so there is nothing to escape.

warehouse.role: Builds the SQL rather than accepting it.
warehouse.why: Membership of an allowlist is the defence, rather than quoting and hoping.

roster.why: "Not decided" and "decided to allow everything" have to look different in a grant.

wh.role: Asked three questions in one call.
wh.why: A 7-day scoped read scans 186,625 bytes; the same read unbounded scans 169 times more.

audit.role: Records the allow, before the rows go back.
audit.why: Warehouse's own log names one service account for everybody. Ours names the person.

person.role: A colleague whose verified email arrives with the call.
person.why: An analyst can count a person across weeks without ever being able to read who they are.

tool.role: One tool call: its arguments, and a declared purpose.
tool.why: Carries the why alongside the what. Only the shape of the call is kept, never the words typed.

gate.role: The roster grant and the domain scope, together.
gate.why: The one component that can turn a call into a refusal, so it is the one that must always log.

decision.role: Allow or deny — who, which tool, the verdict.
decision.why: One person retrying ten times is a conversation. Six people once each is a missing feature.

completion.why: No answer content leaves the process in a log line, whatever the call returned.

outcome.role: The caller's own verdict on whether it worked.
outcome.why: The one thing no instrument can measure. Asked rarely enough to stay answerable.

logging.role: Carries the lines off the box.
logging.why: Measured here as 23 rows carrying 17 distinct insert ids — a 35% over-count if you trust it.

audit.why: Never dedupe on timestamp — two genuine calls in one millisecond would collapse into one.

tracking.role: The one view anything else should query.
tracking.why: The request log carries fields the process never saw, so the join is where the picture completes.
